evidence.excerpt: This paper describes the collection, annotation, and release of a packet-level Modbus/TCP dataset captured on the ICS testbed at the University of Novi Sad. The dataset spans 21 days of normal operation and 6 days of controlled attack execution, comprising approximately 310 million packets. Eight attack scenarios were implemented: function code scanning, coil mass-write injection, replay with modified values, man-in-the-middle payload substitution, time-synchronisation offset injection, denial-of-service flooding, slow-rate polling exhaustion, and firmware update spoofing. Each packet is labelled with a binary normal/attack flag and a scenario identifier. The paper documents the testbed topology, PLC configuration, traffic generation scripts, and labelling methodology in sufficient detail for reproduction. Baseline results for five detectors—statistical process control, one-class SVM, Isolation Forest, autoencoder, and LSTM-based reconstruction—are reported to enable direct comparison by future researchers. The dataset is hosted on the university repository.
